main_text.p: & quis numeret, pauci autem per viam angustam; profer, inquam, stateram, appende: vide contra pau- ca grana, quantam paleam leves. Gregorius Nazianzenus, orat. prima de pa- ce: Melius est vitiosâ concordiâ dis- fidium veritatis causâ ortum. Gregorius Magnus comment. in lib. Reg. Ec- clesia est hæres crucis. Hilarius lib. con- tra Auxentium sub finem: Unum mo- neo, cavete antichristum: male e- nim vos parietum amor cepit, ma- lè ecclesiam Dei in tectis ædificiis- que veneramini, male sub his pacis nomen ingeritis. anne ambiguum est in his antichristum esse fesu- rum? motes mihi, & silvæ, & lacus, & carceres, & voragines sunt tutio- res. in his enim prophetæ, aut ma- nentes aut demersi, Dei spiritu pro- phetabant.
Subscribunt doctores pontificii. Acosta Jesuita de tempore novissimo lib. 1. c. 14. Bella quævis, ex quo homines esse cœperunt, nulla non ætas vidit; ta- men post tempora christiana maxi- me or-

page.notes: The strip at the left edge belongs to the facing page (page 40) and shows tiny marginal text; it is cropped and not transcribed. Doubtful: the page number reads "41" (printed with a low-contrast final digit); the italic/roman split in "Gregorius Magnus comment. in lib. Reg." and the Acosta line is as seen in the scan. No catchword: the page ends on a full line.
